Logistics Reply coordinates robots and workers at The Quality Group’s new facility

The Elsdorf site uses LEA Reply to prioritize tasks and connect conveyors, sorting and packaging as order volumes fluctuate.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗19 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

A newly disclosed fulfilment project

A November 19 release describes Logistics Reply’s implementation at The Quality Group’s new Elsdorf fulfilment centre near Bremen. The 50,000-square-metre facility is designed to process up to 100,000 orders daily. That is a stated capacity, not evidence that this volume is achieved every day.

Allocating work between people and machines

LEA Reply analyzes and prioritizes orders, allocating tasks according to operational needs. Robots perform standardized, physically demanding transport while employees handle complex work and quality assurance. Standard interfaces connect conveyors, sorting and packaging equipment, supporting changing volumes driven by promotional campaigns.

Earlier network results are not site-specific results

The earlier collaboration had LEA in five warehouses by early 2024, with reported delivery-time reductions of nearly 20% and a 99.5% on-time rate. Those figures describe the earlier network, not a separate Elsdorf measurement. The release does not disclose robot counts or site-specific investment returns.
